Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, the team at Acme HealthTech wants to make sure we fully align on how tokens and long-context requests will be billed before the pilot kicks off. I attached our updated pricing sheet (REDCONF-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx) — the key open items I wanted to confirm are: 

- Rounding quantum: do you need us to present examples for fractional tokens or per-request minimums?

- Minimums and credits: can we give a pilot-specific credit or a temporary minimum smoothing?

To move forward quickly: if you can share a 2–3 day sample of typical sessions (one row per request is ideal), we can generate a worked example showing exactly how charges break down. I included a short pilot terms PDF draft for review as well.

Would you be free for a 30-min sync on Thursday to walk through the sample?

Tessa —

Thanks, got the packet. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we send sample data: 

1) When you say "round up to whole tokens", does Redwood bill per generated token only, or do you round the combined input+output to the next whole token? Example: a request with 12.2 input tokens and 3.6 output tokens — what does that become on the invoice?

2) Do streaming responses get billed differently? We have some long in-UI streams (progressive summarization) and I want to make sure we won't be charged repeatedly for repeated prefixes.

3) What is the minimum charge per call? Some of our mobile clients send short prompts very frequently and we'd like to understand if micro-requests trigger minimums that could inflate costs.

Also, any willingness to provide a short-term smoothing credit for the first month while we optimize prompts?

Best,
Jordan

Acme HealthTech

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Sep 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify metering: token rounding, context counting & pilot offer

Tessa / Neha —

Short answers (for customer-facing language):

1) Rounding math: we meter input and output tokens separately and bill the sum. Each side (input, output) is rounded up to the next whole token before summing. Example: 12.2 input -> 13 tokens; 3.6 output -> 4 tokens; invoiceable = 17 tokens. We can also show an example using 4-token rounding quantum if they request bulk bucket math.

2) Streaming: streaming uses the same meter but we do NOT double-bill for prefixes when the client keeps a single session/stream open. We charge for the incremental tokens emitted. If the client reconnects and retransmits the same full prefix as input, that will be billed as a new input. For progressive summarization patterns, recommend keeping a rolling KV cache on the client to avoid re-sending large prefixes.

3) Minimum per-call: default platform minimum is 5 tokens per request (this prevents 0.1-token micro-requests). For enterprise pilots we can raise/lower that floor per negotiated terms. In this account I'd offer a temporary 1-month smoothing credit applied as a monthly invoice offset to cover excessive micro-request noise while they tune (cap at $2,000).

Proposed concession text to Jordan: "We bill input and output tokens separately (each rounded up to whole tokens) and invoice the sum. Streaming is billed incrementally for new tokens only. Our platform applies a 5-token minimum per call by default; for your pilot we can apply a one-month smoothing credit up to $2,000 while you optimize prompt patterns."

If you want we can also offer a pilot discount of 10–12% on token unit price for the first 3 months in exchange for a short usage commitment (e.g., 15M tokens/mo).

—Ben Carter
Director, Pricing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear questions. Confirming Redwood's metering and a pilot offer below (I've copied Ben and Neha). Please find an attached worked example we will generate once you send the sample rows — that will show your exact split.

Metering summary (plain language):
- We meter input tokens and output tokens separately; each side is rounded up to the next whole token before summing. Example: 12.2 input + 3.6 output -> invoiceable = 13 + 4 = 17 tokens.
- Streaming responses are billed only for incremental new tokens emitted while the stream is open; re-sending full prefixes will be billed as new input tokens.
- Platform minimum: default 5-token floor per request. For the pilot, we will waive any micro-request overage up to a $2,000 smoothing credit (applied as invoice offset for month 1) while you optimize prompts.

Pilot commercial offer: 
- 12% discount on token unit price for the first 90 days
- $2,000 smoothing credit for month 1 (as above)
- If you sign the pilot order by 2028-09-15 we'll include a one-time $500 context-bucket credit to offset early long-session churn.

Next steps: send the sample CSV (one row per request, include timestamp, prompt length, expected response length); I will have engineering produce a per-request billing preview within 24 hours. If the pilot offer looks good I'll circulate a DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
